clarification_questions.question: What other dissolved solids, if any, does the solution contain, so that the refractometer reading can be interpreted as sucrose rather than total soluble solids?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: If other solutes vary, a refractometer reference and any spectral calibration track total solids, not sucrose, and the method choice changes.

clarification_questions.why_it_matters: In NIR transmission the optical pathlength must be controlled; too wide loses signal to absorption, too narrow samples a negligible volume.

recommendations.rationale: For a clear, colourless aqueous liquid, NIR transmission with a controlled pathlength (or transflection) is the primary method to test first. Water and sucrose O-H and C-H bands appear in the NIR, and standard silica fibers support the 10 m link.
recommendations.conditions: The optical pathlength must be selected and controlled for 5-15 % w/w sucrose, and calibration must be validated on the actual solution.

risks.risk: The 20-30 °C process temperature span shifts the water and sucrose bands, so temperature compensation or an auxiliary temperature sensor is likely needed.
Daily hot caustic CIP may attack the probe window, seals or fiber, and the sources give no compatibility data for this duty.
If other dissolved solids are present, the refractometer reference and the spectral model track total soluble solids rather than sucrose specifically.

steps.step: Collect representative sucrose solutions spanning 5-15 % w/w and the 20-30 °C temperature span, including any other solutes present in the real stream.
steps.purpose: Cover the expected chemical and physical variation before any calibration is attempted.

steps.step: Measure each sample independently with the laboratory refractometer, and confirm its accuracy against gravimetrically prepared sucrose standards at the 0.3 % w/w limit.
steps.purpose: Establish a trustworthy reference before judging the spectral method.

steps.step: On the bench, acquire NIR transmission spectra at candidate pathlengths and, if available, transflection spectra with the same spectrometer; record solution temperature with each spectrum.
steps.purpose: Select the geometry with adequate signal and sensitivity across the range.

steps.step: Build a chemometric calibration (e.g. PLS) per technique against the refractometer values, with temperature as a variable, and validate on held-out batches not used in calibration.
steps.purpose: Quantify prediction error honestly, including the temperature effect.

steps.step: Go/no-go: the customer defines the criterion, e.g. prediction error within plus or minus 0.3 % w/w on held-out samples at 1-minute acquisition; only if NIR falls short, test Raman as the next single method.
steps.purpose: Give the customer a clear, numeric decision basis for the in-line trial.

feasibility_plan.reference_measurements: Laboratory refractometer on every calibration and validation sample, checked against gravimetric sucrose standards.
feasibility_plan.decision_basis: Customer-defined: prediction error within plus or minus 0.3 % w/w on held-out samples at the required 1-minute cadence.

chemometrics_note: A PLS calibration against the refractometer values is needed because NIR bands are broad and overlapping; include temperature as a variable and validate on held-out batches, since the calibration is specific to this matrix.
realtime_tracking_note: A reading every minute is compatible with NIR diode-array acquisition, which records all wavelengths simultaneously and suits fast processes; the actual cadence depends on the selected instrument.
future_direction: If the trial succeeds, a compact LED-based NIR sensor at selected wavelengths could later replace the full spectrometer for routine monitoring, following the sensor-simplification approach shown in the literature.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the bench trial shows that NIR water absorption or 20-30 °C temperature shifts prevent achieving ±0.3 % w/w, Raman (O2) becomes the choice; if other solutes are present, calibration needs re-evaluation.
proposal.next_step: Test NIR transmission on representative sucrose solutions first, and compare against refractometer readings to verify whether ±0.3 % w/w is achieved.

brief_answer: For a clear aqueous sucrose solution, test NIR transmission with a fiber probe first as the simple, lower-cost option: it is suited to transparent liquids and operates over a 10 m silica link. Raman is recommended as the optimal technical fit if water background shifts prevent reaching plus or minus 0.3 % w/w. Key open items are optical pathlength, pipe fitting, CIP compatibility, and whether other dissolved solids exist.
